newsitem.title: SPAIN: Santander says Chile IPO oversubscribed.
newsitem.headline: Santander says Chile IPO oversubscribed.

text.p: Spain's Banco Santander on Wednesday said an initial public offering of Santander Chile Holding shares on the Santiago stock exchange was oversubscribed and the amount was set after pro-rating at the equivalent of $137 million.

The share offering closed on October 31 with subscriptions totalling $165 million compared with initial expectations of $100-120 million. Individual investors accounted for 74 percent of total demand and institutional investors for the rest.
Santander established the final amount of the IPO above the upper limit that had been set, creating a shareholder base of more than 6,000 investors as a result.

All orders up to 10 million Chilean pesos will be met 100 percent, those between 10 and 70 million will be 77 percent satisfied and those above 70 million 65 percent met. Institutional investor orders will be 72.5 percent satisfied.

The public offering is part of a $290 million capital increase for Santander Chile Holding, the parent company for Santander Group activities in Chile, which represents 27.7 percent of the company's capital to date.
The balance will be subscribed by Banco Santander.
The offering was launched to partly finance the acquisition earlier this year of Banco Osorno y la Union, which was merged into Banco Santander Chile on July 1.
